title: Batista2022: Motor-imagery EEG during NeuRow VR/haptics BCI training
description: EEG recordings from 20 healthy volunteers performing cued left- versus right-hand motor imagery of a bimanual rowing task during brain-computer interface training. Conditions combined Graz and NeuRow virtual-reality feedback with optional haptic and head-mounted-display feedback. Alongside 32-channel EEG, the dataset includes ECG, respiration, and auxiliary channels, and is intended for neurorehabilitation-oriented BCI research.
methods_description: Data were recorded in a single lab session per subject using a Brain Products LiveAmp 32 with actiCAP active Ag/AgCl electrodes (32 EEG channels, 500 Hz) in BrainVision format. Each session had up to five imagery runs (MI, MIMO, MIMOHP, MIMOVR, MIMOVRHP), each with cue-locked 5 s left/right-hand motor imagery trials.
